Reset this setting to its default value? Its line is commented out in the termux.properties file, so the app uses the default again.
Logs will not have entries for terminal view keys. (Default)
Logcat logs will have entries for terminal view keys. These are very verbose and should be disabled under normal circumstances or will cause performance issues.
Disable flashes and notifications for plugin errors.
Show flashes and notifications for plugin errors. (Default)
Soft Keyboard Only If No Hardware
Soft keyboard will be enabled even if hardware keyboard is connected. (Default)
Soft keyboard will be enabled only if no hardware keyboard is connected.
The status bar is shown above the terminal and the terminal is laid out below it. (Default)
The status bar is hidden and the terminal is laid out behind it, so that it uses the whole screen.
Enabled, which adds extra insets to the terminal to try to fix it being drawn below the status bar area. Only used when the fullscreen mode is also enabled.
The edge handle, the edge swipe, both or neither
Height of the terminal toolbar as a percentage of its default height. The default value is 100 and the allowed range is 40 to 300.
Key labels are shown as defined in the `extra-keys` property.
Key labels are automatically converted to uppercase. (Default)
IMEs like Gboard may only show an ASCII QWERTY keyboard in the terminal view, so CJK keyboards like Chinese Pinyin cannot be used directly.
IMEs like Gboard can use CJK keyboards like Chinese Pinyin in the terminal view. Suggestions are disabled for other languages and the keyboard may restart when the input language is changed.
Characters are sent to the terminal as they are committed by the input method. (Default)
A visible password input type is used, which fixes characters not being sent until enter is pressed on some keyboards, like the Samsung one.
Enabled, which fixes Ctrl+Space not working to switch the input method on some ROMs, but may break it on other devices.
Scroll to the previous command (shell integration)
Scroll to the next command (shell integration)

The keys that will be sent to the terminal when the
corresponding action is "Send a key sequence". The keys must be
separated by spaces and use the same names as the `extra-keys`
property, like ESC, TAB, PGUP, UP, F1 or CTRL c.

A key may be prefixed with CTRL, ALT, SHIFT or FN to apply it as a
modifier to the next key only, so "CTRL c" is Ctrl+C while
"CTRL c d" is Ctrl+C followed by D.
Reset the volume key actions to their default values, so that the volume keys behave like the upstream termux app again. The actions are only used when the volume keys behaviour above is \"Virtual\".
Volume key actions were reset to their default values
The soft keyboard state is not changed when the app starts. (Default)
The soft keyboard is hidden when the app starts.
Hide Extra Keys When Keyboard Hidden
The extra keys row is kept visible while the soft keyboard is hidden. (Default)

The extra keys row is hidden while the soft keyboard is hidden, so that the terminal gets its rows, and is shown again when the soft keyboard is shown. Requires Android 6 or later. The toolbar can still be shown manually, which is kept until the soft keyboard visibility changes again.
Dragging with a finger sends scroll wheel events to terminal programs that use mouse tracking. (Default)

Dragging with a finger is reported as a drag of the mouse pointer, which programs that support dragging, like for selecting text or resizing panes in a TUI, can handle. Scrolling with a drag is then not reported as scroll wheel events to programs that use mouse tracking.
Taps with a mouse or while mouse tracking is active are forwarded to the terminal and do not show the soft keyboard. (Default)
The soft keyboard is shown for those taps too, which can be convenient, but may conflict with terminal programs that use mouse tracking or clicking, like TUIs.
Shortcuts like Ctrl+Alt+C to create a new session are handled by the app. (Default)
The key combinations are sent to the terminal instead, so that the app does not intercept them.
How the buttons of the extra keys row are shown
Only the key of the button is shown, the key sent by swiping up on it is not indicated.
The key sent by swiping up on a button is also shown in a small font in its top right corner, like END on the right arrow key. (Default)
The buttons have no visible background, like in the upstream Termux app.
A rounded tile is drawn behind each button, like for the keys of the Gboard keyboard. The colors follow the color scheme. (Default)
Colors of the extra keys row drawn below the terminal, which follow the termux color scheme by default

$PREFIX and $HOME will be overwritten with the contents of the selected backup, and the current environment will be backed up first. You can still cancel the restore in the terminal afterwards.
Terminal margin adjustment will be disabled.

Terminal margin adjustment will be enabled. It should be enabled to try to fix the issue where soft keyboard covers part of extra keys/terminal view. If it causes screen flickering on your devices, then disable it. (Default)
A horizontal swipe on the terminal does not switch the session.
A horizontal swipe on the terminal switches to the previous or next session. It is not used while selecting text or while a terminal program is using mouse tracking. (Default)
In dp units, 0–100. Insets the terminal grid from the window edge, like the padding of Windows Terminal. The terminal toolbar and the sessions drawer are not padded.
Terminal programs may write the clipboard (Default)
Terminal programs may read and write the clipboard (Less secure, a remote shell could read everything you copied)

Adds OSC 133 command marks to ~/.bashrc (and ~/.zshrc if it exists), so that commands can be jumped to, tapped on the right edge and seen when they fail. Open a new session or run `source ~/.bashrc` to apply it.
The installed shell integration is older than the one of the app. Install it again so that the notification cards show the command that was run.
